description: We are building a portable EWOD microfluidic platform for rapid DNA/RNA isothermal LAMP assays. Powered via USB-C with custom PCB controls and optical sensing, it automates droplet control to detect pathogens, viral infections, and genetic health markers without heavy lab gear. Seeking software, hardware, & human-factors teammates to build this space-grade diagnostic monitor!
summary:
We developed Portable Health & DNA Diagnostics, a compact, automated microfluidic platform designed to monitor astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Using electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD) technology, our system moves tiny liquid droplets across custom PCB electrode arrays using electrical fields instead of mechanical pumps. Integrated with isothermal Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) assays, the platform performs rapid DNA and RNA analysis to detect pathogens, viral infections, and health markers using only microliters of sample.   
     This project addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge by providing astronauts with an autonomous, point-of-care health tool for closed spacecraft environments. Long-duration spaceflight exposes crews to radiation, altered gravity, and immune shifts, making rapid self-assessment critical. Unlike traditional labs requiring heavy machinery and days of waiting, our USB-C powered device automates fluid control, minimizes contamination, and delivers actionable readouts to protect crew safety far from Earth.   
     The system features replaceable daughterboards, precise regulation for 60 - 65 degrees Celsius amplification, and optical/colorimetric sensing for microgravity use. Combining embedded microcontroller logic with robust design, our solution empowers crew members to manage health risks and maintain mission readiness.
details:
Portable Health & DNA Diagnostics is a compact, automated microfluidic platform designed to function as a miniature, handheld diagnostic laboratory. Rather than relying on mechanical pumps or bulky benchtop equipment, the system utilizes electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD) technology to precisely move, mix, and manipulate tiny liquid droplets of sample across custom printed circuit board (PCB) electrode arrays using electrical fields within a protective oil reservoir. Integrated with Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) assays, the platform maintains a constant temperature between 60 - 65 degrees Celsius on a swappable daughterboard to amplify target DNA or RNA sequences. Pathogen detection and successful amplification are read out via optical and colorimetric sensors or visual dye changes, which communicate results back to a computer dashboard through a USB-C connection.

The intended impact of this project is to provide rapid, point-of-care testing that eliminates the days-long shipping and processing delays associated with traditional centralized laboratories. Designed specifically for closed spacecraft environments, long-duration space missions, and resource-limited settings where heavy machinery is impractical, the platform delivers actionable diagnostic results in 20 to 60 minutes. By automating droplet control and isolating samples within a sealed enclosure and oil pool, the design minimizes manual handling risks and contamination, offering a cost-effective and scalable alternative to expensive lab equipment.

To develop this project, a diverse suite of hardware, software, and consumable resources was utilized. The physical hardware and fabrication stack features custom PCB electrode arrays, a Voltera V-One PCB printer using silver nanoparticle conductive ink, a spin coater for applying uniform Cytonix FluoroPel hydrophobic coatings, 3D-printed modular enclosures and oil barriers, digital multimeters, waveform generators, and a USB-C power and data interface. Software development relied on KiCAD for electrode array design, Altium Designer for motherboard development, a Nucleo microcontroller for hardware control, and C/C++ or Python environments running a custom serial command GUI. Essential testing consumables included 0.9% sodium chloride, silicone and safflower oils, FluoroPel 800 2.0%, and standard LAMP assay reagents containing Bst DNA polymerase and specific primers.

The project demonstrates creativity by bridging solid-state electronics with molecular biology, transforming a standard printed circuit board into an active laboratory surface where electrical forces directly manipulate chemical droplets. Moving beyond conventional fluidic plumbing, the system introduces a modular, credit-card-style swappable daughterboard architecture. This innovation allows a single electronic motherboard to perform entirely different diagnostic assays simply by exchanging the active test surface.

Several critical design factors were carefully evaluated during development to ensure safety, reliability, and usability. Electrical safety and power efficiency were prioritized by designing around low-voltage operation and USB-C power delivery to fit within strict spacecraft power budgets under 5 watts. Material compatibility and thin-film durability guided by standards like ASTM D882 were assessed to prevent electrode degradation and dielectric breakdown during saline electrolysis and oil flooding. Furthermore, the team engineered precise thermal management controls to maintain the strict 60 - 65 degrees Celsius threshold required for LAMP amplification without overheating sensitive driver components, while focusing on human factors and ergonomics to ensure intuitive operation for non-technical users or astronauts.
